data.long_meaning: In Christian tradition, Dismas is one of the two thieves crucified with Jesus. He is also known as the Good Thief for his repentance and faith. The name Dismas carries the meaning “Good Thief” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Dismas usually hope their child will grow to embody good thief and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: דיסמס
in_hebrew.meaning: שם של אחד הגנבים על הצלב עם ישו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דיסמס הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'אחד משני הגנבים שנצלבו עם ישו'. השם מוזכר בברית החדשה כגנב ששינה את דרכיו והתחרט על מעשיו לפני מותו. הדיסמס הקדוש הוא דמות חשובה במסורת הנוצרית והוא נחשב לקדוש מעונה.

in_greek.name: Δυσμάς
in_greek.meaning: Όνομα του ενός από τους δύο ληστές που σταυρώθηκαν με τον Ιησού
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Δυσμάς είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και αναφέρεται στον έναν από τους δύο ληστές που σταυρώθηκαν μαζί με τον Ιησού Χριστό. Η ιστορία του Δυσμάς είναι γνωστή από το Ευαγγέλιο του Λουκά και έχει μεγάλη σημασία στην χριστιανική παράδοση ως σύμβολο της μετάνοιας και της σωτηρίας.

in_latin.name: Dismas
in_latin.meaning: Name of one of the two thieves crucified with Jesus Christ
in_latin.long_meaning: Dismas is a name derived from the Greek language, referring to one of the two thieves who were crucified alongside Jesus Christ. The story of Dismas is recorded in the New Testament and holds significant importance in Christian tradition as a symbol of repentance and salvation. The name Dismas has been used in various Christian cultures to signify the power of redemption.

in_english.name: Dismas
in_english.meaning: One of the two thieves crucified with Jesus, symbolizing repentance
in_english.long_meaning: The name Dismas originates from the Greek language and refers to one of the two thieves crucified alongside Jesus Christ. According to the New Testament, specifically in the Gospel of Luke, Dismas repented and asked Jesus for mercy before his death. This act of repentance has made Dismas a significant figure in Christian tradition, symbolizing the possibility of redemption and forgiveness. The name Dismas is often chosen for its spiritual connotations and historical significance in Christian culture.

He has been portrayed as a model of contrition, penitence, and faith, inspiring many to reflect on the redemptive power of Christ's sacrifice and the possibility of repentance and salvation for all, even criminals or sinners.
data.spiritual_significance: Dismas represents the transformative power of faith and conversion, emphasizing the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning toward God – no matter the circumstances, background, or actions of one's life. It serves as a reminder that it's never too late to ask for mercy and embrace the love and grace offered by God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dismas, the Good Thief, represents redemption and forgiveness. He was crucified alongside Jesus, acknowledging his sins and asking for mercy, receiving it in the form of salvation. His story underscores the transformative power of faith and repentance.

biblical_reference.note: Dismas is mentioned in the New Testament as one of the thieves crucified with Jesus.

historical_references.reference: Tradition holds that Dismas was the name of the Good Thief, crucified next to Jesus. According to the New Testament, when the Romans were dividing up the condemned men's garments, the repentant thief asked Jesus to remember him in paradise. Jesus promised that he would be with him in paradise that very day. This conversion and promise are believed to have occurred around 30 AD during the period of Jesus' crucifixion and death.

The name Dismas, which may mean 'of the same status' or 'the son of a rich man', became associated with the Good Thief due to a late medieval legend. In this legend, Dismas was a nobleman who had been falsely accused of treason and sentenced to death. He was crucified next to Jesus and repented at the last moment. This legend gained popularity in the 15th century and contributed to the veneration of the Good Thief in Christian tradition.
historical_references.context: Late medieval legend and veneration of the Good Thief

The trends surrounding Dismas include themes such as penitence, compassion, forgiveness, redemption, and the power of repentance. In contemporary art, the image of the penitent thief is often used to inspire reflection and contemplation on themes of sin, redemption, and the human condition.
